issues.legal_issue: The prohibition on compelling public servants to produce assessment records covers statements made by persons other than the person whose assessment was being conducted.
material_facts: In a civil suit concerning repayment of a loan, the defendant sought production of an official record containing a statement allegedly made by the plaintiff during assessment proceedings concerning the defendant.
The Commissioner of Income-tax objected to producing the record, and the statement was not within any of the specified exceptions to the statutory confidentiality provisions.
issues.conclusion: The court could not require the public servant to produce the statement; the prohibition applied even though the statement had been made by someone other than the person whose assessment was involved.
issues.legal_principle: Section 54(1) of the Indian Income-tax Act, 1922, treats information and evidence in assessment proceedings as confidential and, notwithstanding the Indian Evidence Act, prevents a court from requiring a public servant to produce the relevant records or give evidence about them, subject to the specified exceptions in section 54(3); section 54(2) penalizes disclosure. Buchibai v. Nagpur University, Rama Rao v. Venkataramayya, Suraj Narain v. Seth Jhabhu Lal and Others, and Banarsi Devi v. Janki Devi concerned the admissibility of certified copies or evidence and did not decide whether a court could compel production of original records.

rule.if: civil_evidence_request and official_assessment_record and statement_by_person_other_than_assessee and record_outside_exceptions

predicates.civil_evidence_request: A party in a civil case asked the court to obtain evidence for use in the case.
predicates.official_assessment_record: The requested material was an official record created or kept in the course of a person's tax assessment proceedings.
predicates.statement_by_person_other_than_assessee: The record contained a statement made by someone other than the person whose assessment proceedings produced the record.
predicates.record_outside_exceptions: The requested material did not fall within an express exception to the confidentiality treatment of assessment material.

issues.definition: When a party seeks official assessment material for evidence in a civil case, a statement by someone other than the person assessed remains within the material that the court cannot compel a public servant to produce if no express exception applies.

issues.legal_issue: An assessee's waiver does not remove the prohibition on a court compelling production of assessment material by a public servant.
material_facts: The defendant sought an official record containing a statement allegedly made during assessment proceedings relating to the defendant.
The defendant asserted that the confidentiality protection existed for the assessee's benefit and that the defendant waived it.
issues.conclusion: The asserted waiver did not make the prohibition in section 54 inoperative; the court could not compel production of the record.
issues.legal_principle: Section 54 of the Indian Income-tax Act, 1922, contains no express or implied exception permitting an assessee to waive the prohibition. The prohibition against a court requiring a public servant to produce covered material is absolute. Buchibai v. Nagpur University addressed the admissibility of a certified copy, not whether waiver permits compelled production of an original record; the other cited decisions on certified copies likewise did not decide that question.

predicates.civil_evidence_request: A party in a civil case asked the court to obtain evidence for use in the case.
predicates.official_assessment_record: The requested material was an official record created or kept in the course of a person's tax assessment proceedings.
predicates.assessee_claimed_waiver: The person whose assessment proceedings produced the record asserted that the confidentiality protection had been waived.

issues.definition: When a party seeks an official assessment record for evidence in a civil case, the court cannot compel a public servant to produce it even if the person assessed claims to waive confidentiality.
